name: CREW-MUSTER-the-side-read-without-a-muster
old: const way = muster && (ctx.way === 'board' || ctx.way === 'repel') ? ctx.way : null;
new: const way = ctx.way === 'board' || ctx.way === 'repel' ? ctx.way : null;
why: Belt and braces: the one producer of ctx.way, world.js navalCrewFrame, names a side only with a boarding's own muster (`if (toward)`, the same frame that sets ctx.muster to +1 or -1), and resets it to null every call - so no step ever carries a way without a muster, and the guard never decides. It stays so a direct caller (a test, a future host) cannot make a crew at peace cry a muster's words.
